findings.failure_scenario: The diff renamed get(Object object) to get(Object target) but left `return UnsafeMemory.unsafeGetObject(object, getOffset());` unchanged; 'object' resolves to nothing (no such field in UnsafeFieldInfo/VanillaFieldInfo/AbstractFieldInfo), so javac fails with 'cannot find symbol: variable object' and the module cannot be built at all.
findings.summary: The parameter rename object->target left the getter body referencing the undefined identifier 'object', so the file no longer compiles.

findings.failure_scenario: Compiling the project after this change fails with 'cannot find symbol: variable object' in IntFieldInfo.getInt; every int field read via FieldInfo is impossible until fixed.
findings.summary: getInt(Object target) still calls UnsafeMemory.unsafeGetInt(object, getOffset()) with an undefined 'object' identifier after the rename, breaking compilation.

findings.failure_scenario: Calling fieldInfo.set(tupleProxy, 42) (or the char/long/double overload) executes set(name, (Object) 42), which invokes getMap(name) -> Proxy.getInvocationHandler("fieldName") on a String; Proxy.getInvocationHandler throws IllegalArgumentException('not a proxy instance'), so primitive values can never be written to tuple-backed fields even though the renamed 'target' parameter is ignored.
findings.summary: TupleFieldInfo's primitive set overloads (char/int/long/double) pass the field-name String 'name' instead of the 'target' proxy to set(), so any primitive write to a tuple field throws IllegalArgumentException.

findings.failure_scenario: The public FieldInfo javadoc (lines 35, 71, 137, 237-238) is rendered garbled in the published API docs: 'This metadata is used by WireMarshaller ... to read and write field newValues' and 'It's a shallow copy, so targets will be copied by reference' misstate what the API does, misleading all consumers of the javadoc.
findings.summary: The mechanical rename corrupted published API javadoc prose: 'read and write field newValues', 'FieldInfo targets', 'Returns the newValue of the field', and 'targets will be copied by reference' are nonsensical replacements of 'values'/'objects'.

findings.failure_scenario: Running the javadoc tool emits a 'parameter o not found' warning for getMap(Object target), and the generated documentation for TupleFieldInfo.getMap documents a parameter that does not exist.
findings.summary: The javadoc tag '@param o The object whose fields map needs to be fetched' was not updated when the parameter was renamed to 'target', so the tag references a nonexistent parameter.
